text:
Less than two weeks after Florida Politics reported that a brief 2025 party switch likely bars him from running as a Democrat in Florida’s 28th Congressional District, Hector Mujica is on the precipice of withdrawing from the race.

He wants former federal prosecutor Robin Peguero, a candidate in Florida’s 27th Congressional District, to switch races and replace him, multiple sources confirmed.

Florida Politics has reached out to Mujica and Peguero’s campaigns for comment and will update this report when they respond.

Voter registration records in Broward County, where Mujica lives, show he changed his party affiliation from Democrat to no party affiliation on June 4, 2025, before switching back to Democrat on July 26, 2025.

To run for a party’s nomination, candidates in Florida must be registered members of that party for 365 consecutive days, per a state statute Democratic lawmakers updated with unanimous support in the Legislature this year. Gov. Ron DeSantis signed the measure in early April.

Mujica, a former Google executive, has denied changing his party affiliation or knowing about the change until late last month, when the campaign of his Primary opponent in CD 28, retired Air Force Commander Phil Ehr, flagged the issue.

Mujica and his campaign did not explain why neither he nor anyone working for him discovered the problem during his prior U.S. Senate bid, which he left about two weeks before the race’s qualifying period began, or until late last month.

A spokesperson for Mujica, who raised more than $717,000 and spent close to $640,000 on the aborted Senate race, initially attributed the registration issue to a “clerical or administrative error.” But the Broward Supervisor of Elections disputed that explanation, saying that a review of its records “found no evidence” of any such mistake.

Ehr, who ran unsuccessfully against incumbent U.S. Rep. Carlos Giménez in CD 28 last cycle, filed a complaint against Mujica with the Florida Elections Commission. He said he would sue Mujica on Monday, the first day of qualifying, to block Mujica from the ballot.

Vanessa Brito, Ehr’s campaign manager, said the camp will instead file the lawsuit Friday, the last day of qualifying, if Mujica remains in the race.

Brito told Florida Politics she knows Mujica is trying to recruit Peguero — who raised $800,000 through March 31 and currently faces Eliott Rodriguez in a Democratic Primary for CD 27, where Republican U.S. Rep. María Elvira Salazar is defending — to run in CD 28.

She said the move “disgusted” her.

“At this point, they should probably leave it alone,” she said. “I encourage (Mujica) to do the right thing, not hurt himself, the donors or the campaign any further, and wait until he is eligible.”

CD 28 covers portions of southwestern Miami-Dade County — including all or part of Florida City, Homestead, South Miami and Sweetwater and a slew of unincorporated neighborhoods like Kendall, Goulds, the Hammocks and Westchester — and all of the Florida Keys in Monroe County.

CD 27 spans Miami, Coral Gables, Cutler Bay, Key Biscayne, Pinecrest, North Bay Village, South Miami, West Miami and several unincorporated areas.

Ehr lives in CD 28, while Peguero lives in CD 27. Notably, federal officials from Florida must only live in the state, not the district they represent, to qualify for office.
